First, the oil is separated by mixing it with water—kind of like putting the apples in the basket with water—until it becomes a thick liquid called crude oil.

Next, that crude oil is fed into a big tank called a "refinery," which feels like laying out slices of the apple basket in a big pile to get all the apples inside. Inside the tank, the crude oil is heated and mixed with a special water called "liquiator steam."
